title: Boss: a day on certificate duty
summary: Four tickets from a real week: inspect, issue from a CSR, package a PFX, and diagnose a broken server, each the .NET twin of the commands you now know.

steps.title: Your queue
body: Four tickets are waiting. Each is a command you would type in the field; you will build its .NET twin so you understand exactly what it does.
1. **"What's on this cert?"** Print it like `openssl x509 -noout -subject -issuer -dates -fingerprint -sha256 -ext subjectAltName`.
2. **"Please sign our CSR."** Issue from a CSR like `openssl x509 -req -copy_extensions copy -extfile leaf.ext`, safely, and hand back `fullchain.pem`.
3. **"IIS needs a PFX."** `openssl pkcs12 -export -in cert.pem -inkey key.pem`, refusing a key that doesn't match.
4. **"The API is broken for some clients."** Diagnose a server from what it sends and what the client trusts.

steps.title: Ticket 1: openssl x509, in .NET
prompt: Write `string Describe(X509Certificate2 cert)` returning these lines joined with `\n`:
```text
subject=CN=shop.example
issuer=CN=Dojo Issuing CA
notBefore=Jan  1 00:00:00 2030 GMT
notAfter=Jan  1 00:00:00 2031 GMT
sha256 Fingerprint=3A:F1:...:9E
X509v3 Subject Alternative Name:
DNS:shop.example, DNS:www.shop.example
- dates in UTC, day right-aligned in two characters
- fingerprint: SHA-256 of `RawData`, upper-case hex pairs joined by `:`
- the last two lines only if the certificate has a SAN (4 spaces of indent, `DNS:` before each name, joined by `, `)
hints: Reuse your date format from lesson 1: `$"{t:MMM} {t.Day,2} {t:HH:mm:ss yyyy} GMT"`.
`cert.Extensions.OfType<X509SubjectAlternativeNameExtension>().FirstOrDefault()` is null when there is no SAN.
template: var dojoRoot = DojoCert("CN=Dojo Root", null, true, naYear: 2040);
var dojoInt = DojoCert("CN=Dojo Issuing CA", dojoRoot, true);
var dojoLeaf = DojoCert("CN=shop.example", dojoInt, false, "shop.example,www.shop.example", nbYear: 2030, naYear: 2031);

Dojo.Eq("a leaf with SANs", "subject=CN=shop.example
issuer=CN=Dojo Issuing CA
notBefore=Jan  1 00:00:00 2030 GMT
notAfter=Jan  1 00:00:00 2031 GMT
sha256 Fingerprint=" + DojoFp(dojoLeaf) + "
X509v3 Subject Alternative Name:
    DNS:shop.example, DNS:www.shop.example", Describe(dojoLeaf));

Dojo.Eq("a root without a SAN", "subject=CN=Dojo Root
issuer=CN=Dojo Root
notBefore=Jan  1 00:00:00 2030 GMT
notAfter=Jan  1 00:00:00 2040 GMT
sha256 Fingerprint=" + DojoFp(dojoRoot), Describe(dojoRoot));
static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);

steps.title: Ticket 2: sign a CSR, copy only its SAN
prompt: Write `string IssueFullchain(string csrPem, X509Certificate2 ca)` returning the `fullchain.pem` text for the requester.

The requester put their names in the CSR, so copy extensions like `-copy_extensions copy`, but **safely**: load with `CertificateRequestLoadOptions.UnsafeLoadCertificateExtensions`, then **remove every requested extension except the SAN** (OID `2.5.29.17`). A CSR asking for `CA:TRUE` must not get it. Then add:
- Basic Constraints not a CA (critical), Key Usage `DigitalSignature` (critical), EKU serverAuth, AKI from `ca`
- valid **2030-01-01 to 2031-01-01 UTC**, serial `new byte[] { 0x51 }`
Return `leaf.ExportCertificatePem() + "\n" + ca.ExportCertificatePem()` (leaf first, the CA second, no root).
starter: // keep only the SAN, add the CA's extensions, sign, build the PEM
solution: req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid("1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1") }, false));
hints: `req.CertificateExtensions` is a `Collection<X509Extension>`: filter it to a list, `Clear()`, and add back what you keep.
Build the chain text with `ExportCertificatePem()` for the leaf, then the CA.
template: var dojoRoot = DojoCert("CN=Dojo Root", null, true, nbYear: 2029, naYear: 2040);
var dojoCa = DojoCert("CN=Dojo Issuing CA", dojoRoot, true, nbYear: 2029, naYear: 2035);
var dojoReq = new CertificateRequest("CN=shop.example", dojoKey, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
var dojoSanB = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); dojoSanB.AddDnsName("shop.example"); dojoSanB.AddDnsName("www.shop.example");
Dojo.Eq("then the issuing CA", "CN=Dojo Issuing CA", dojoBundle[1].Subject);
Dojo.Eq("SAN copied from the CSR", "shop.example,www.shop.example", san == null ? "" : string.Join(",", san.EnumerateDnsNames()));
Dojo.Check("exactly one Basic Constraints, not a CA (the CSR's CA:TRUE was dropped)", bcs.Count == 1 && !bcs[0].CertificateAuthority, "remove every requested extension except 2.5.29.17");
Dojo.Check("validates for serverAuth", DojoValid(dojoRoot, leaf, new X509Certificate2Collection { dojoBundle[1] }), "check the extensions and dates");
bool DojoValid(X509Certificate2 root, X509Certificate2 leaf, X509Certificate2Collection extra)
static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);

steps.title: Ticket 3: openssl pkcs12 -export
prompt: Write `byte[] BuildPfx(string certPem, string keyPem, string password)`, the twin of
```bash
openssl pkcs12 -export -in cert.pem -inkey key.pem -out site.pfx
- load the certificate from `certPem` and the ECDSA key from `keyPem` (`ECDsa.Create()` then `ImportFromPem`)
- if the key does not match the certificate's public key, throw `InvalidOperationException("key values mismatch")` (nginx's words)
- otherwise attach the key with `CopyWithPrivateKey` and export PKCS#12 with `password`
starter: byte[] BuildPfx(string certPem, string keyPem, string password)
solution: byte[] BuildPfx(string certPem, string keyPem, string password)
hints: Compare `ExportSubjectPublicKeyInfo()` from both sides, as in lesson 5.
template: var dojoReq = new CertificateRequest("CN=iis.shop.example", dojoKey, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
using var dojoCert = dojoReq.CreateSelfSigned(new DateTimeOffset(2030, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero), new DateTimeOffset(2031, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero));
Dojo.Eq("PFX holds the private key", true, dojoBack.HasPrivateKey);
Dojo.Throws<InvalidOperationException>("a key from another pair is refused", () => BuildPfx(dojoCertPem, dojoWrongKey, "iis-pw"));
static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);

steps.title: Ticket 4: diagnose the server
prompt: Write `List<string> Diagnose(X509Certificate2 leaf, X509Certificate2Collection sent, X509Certificate2Collection trusted, string host)`.

`sent` is what the server sends **after** the leaf (intermediates, maybe the root); `trusted` is the client's trust store (possibly empty). Build an `X509Chain` with `CustomRootTrust`, serverAuth, no revocation, no downloads, `VerificationTime` 2030-06-01 UTC, and return the problems in this order:
| Problem | When |
| `missing intermediate` | `PartialChain` and `sent` has no CA certificate that isn't self-signed |
| `untrusted root` | `UntrustedRoot`, or `PartialChain` while an intermediate was sent |
| `expired` | `NotTimeValid` (expired or not yet valid: both count) |
| `wrong EKU` | `NotValidForUsage` |
| `name mismatch` | `host` not in the SAN (`MatchesHostname`, no CN fallback) |
An empty list means healthy. Then you know which command to run: `cat leaf.pem int.pem > fullchain.pem`, `update-ca-certificates`, a renewal, or a reissue with `-addext`.
starter: List<string> Diagnose(X509Certificate2 leaf, X509Certificate2Collection sent, X509Certificate2Collection trusted, string host)
solution: List<string> Diagnose(X509Certificate2 leaf, X509Certificate2Collection sent, X509Certificate2Collection trusted, string host)
if (!leaf.MatchesHostname(host, allowWildcards: true, allowCommonName: false)) problems.Add("name mismatch");
hints: An intermediate is a sent certificate whose subject differs from its issuer.
Collect the flags into a set: `chain.ChainStatus.Select(s => s.Status).ToHashSet()`.
Check in the table's order and `Add` each label.
template: var dojoRoot = DojoCert("CN=Shop Root CA", null, true, naYear: 2040);
var dojoInt = DojoCert("CN=Shop Issuing CA", dojoRoot, true, naYear: 2035);
Dojo.Eq("healthy", new List<string>(), Diagnose(dojoGood, dojoSendInt, dojoTrust, "www.shop.example"));
Dojo.Eq("leaf only", new List<string> { "missing intermediate" }, Diagnose(dojoGood, dojoNone, dojoTrust, "shop.example"));
Dojo.Eq("root sent but not trusted", new List<string> { "untrusted root" }, Diagnose(dojoGood, new X509Certificate2Collection { dojoInt, dojoRoot }, dojoNone, "shop.example"));
Dojo.Eq("intermediate sent, nothing trusted", new List<string> { "untrusted root" }, Diagnose(dojoGood, dojoSendInt, dojoNone, "shop.example"));
Dojo.Eq("not yet valid counts as expired, plus a wrong name", new List<string> { "expired", "name mismatch" }, Diagnose(dojoEarly, dojoSendInt, dojoTrust, "shop.example"));
Dojo.Eq("clientAuth certificate on a web server", new List<string> { "wrong EKU" }, Diagnose(dojoClient, dojoSendInt, dojoTrust, "shop.example"));

Dojo.Eq("CN alone does not match", new List<string> { "name mismatch" }, Diagnose(DojoCert("CN=api.shop.example", dojoInt, false, "shop.example", "1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1", 2030, 2031), dojoSendInt, dojoTrust, "api.shop.example"));

req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);
